subject: Clarifying cloud subservice boundary, evidence needs, and bridge letter window
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@shoreline.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying cloud subservice boundary, evidence needs, and bridge letter window

Carlos —

Thanks for taking the time on our SOC 2 evidence request. A few specific asks from our auditor and internal controls team so we can map Shoreline as a subservice organization (or confirm a carve-out):

- Can you confirm the exact audit period covered by your SOC 2 Type II report (report filename, control period start/end)? We need the dates for our mapping (auditor asked for explicit control window).
- Which cloud infrastructure provider(s) did you rely on (AWS/GCP/Azure)? If you rely on a cloud provider's SOC reports as part of your control set, please state whether those are provided as a carve-out or inclusive (i.e., did your auditor carve out the cloud provider controls?).
- Please attach a current list of subprocessors (name, service, purpose, country) and call out any third parties that handle customer data flows.
- Our auditor typically wants a bridge letter when the customer's audit window extends beyond the subservice org report period. Can Shoreline provide a bridge letter covering any gap between your last SOC report and our audit period (we expect our audit window to include Apr 1–Jun 30, 2027 in some requests)? If so, please indicate the earliest you can provide it and what it will state (control continuity, no material changes, etc.).
- For evidence: auditors often request configuration snapshots (IAM org summary, network segmentation diagrams), sample change control tickets, and evidence of monitoring/alerting. Which artifacts can you provide directly, and which artifacts we should request from your cloud provider(s)?

We appreciate a zip of the SOC 2 report and a subprocessors spreadsheet if available. If you prefer, you can also point us to a secure link. Timeline: our auditor would like initial evidence by May 24 to keep the engagement on schedule.

Thanks — cc'ing Vanessa and Rishi from Redwood's compliance team to make sure we capture everything.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@shoreline.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@shoreline.io
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying cloud subservice boundary, evidence needs, and bridge letter window

Hi Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers below and I'm attaching the items we can share immediately.

Attachments: Shoreline_SOC2_Report_10-2026_03-2027.pdf (pdf, SOC 2 Type II), Shoreline_Subprocessors_202705.xlsx (spreadsheet), Bridge_Letter_Q2-2027.pdf (draft bridge letter)

- SOC 2 period: 2026-10-01 through 2027-03-31 (see attached SOC report cover).
- Cloud providers: primary infrastructure on AWS; we use a handful of managed services (RDS, S3, KMS, EKS). Our auditor treated AWS as a carve-out for provider-level controls; we have a mapping that calls out which controls rely on AWS documentation.
- Subprocessors: attached spreadsheet lists all subprocessors, purpose, and data categories.
- Bridge letter: we can provide a bridge letter that affirms no material changes to our control environment since 2027-03-31 and references AWS as a subservice with carve-out scope. Draft is attached; final will be on Shoreline letterhead and signed by our Head of Security.
- Evidence: we can provide configuration exports (IAM trust relationships, S3 bucket policy listings), SOC mappings, and sample change-control tickets. For provider-level evidence (EC2 host configs, hypervisor controls), you will need to reference AWS's SOC 2 report for those controls. I can also include a short mapping file showing which control IDs rely on provider artifacts versus Shoreline-owned controls.

Timeline: I can share the signed bridge letter and final mapping by May 25; configuration snapshots (sanitized) and tickets by May 27. If you need anything faster let me know and we can prioritize.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps — available Fri morning PST.

Regards,
Carlos Mendez
Head of Security Operations
Shoreline Technologies
c.mendez@shoreline.io

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Clarifying cloud subservice boundary, evidence needs, and bridge letter window

Thanks — quick summary and next steps from ops/compliance POV: 

1) Acceptability: We can accept a carve-out for AWS controls provided: the bridge letter explicitly states the control continuity, the SOC 2 report period is documented (they gave 2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31), and we have a mapping that shows which control IDs depend on AWS artifacts. Our auditor wants that mapping to be machine-readable (spreadsheet) and to include reference links to the underlying AWS SOC report sections.

2) Evidence matrix: I started a copy of Evidence Matrix v2 (internal link) — populate the matrix with the subprocessors file and mark any gaps. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cEvidenceMatrix

3) Bridge letter language: Rishi, when you review the draft, please ensure it includes: (a) explicit date range it covers, (b) statement of "no material changes" to control environment or an explicit list of changes, and (c) a clause that references AWS as a subservice and identifies which services are carved out. If Shoreline can't include c), we'll treat AWS controls as not in-scope and request additional compensating evidence from Shoreline.

4) Owner & deadlines: Kimberly will own liaison with Shoreline. Rishi to complete review by EOD May 24. Vanessa will consolidate evidence matrix by EOD May 27. Lauren to sign off once matrix shows no critical gaps.

If they can provide the signed bridge letter on the 25th and the mapping and sanitized configs by the 27th we should be good to meet the auditor's timeline.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Manager, Customer Compliance
Redwood Inference
